hero.lead: A nation of 14.6 million on hills three-quarters farmed, that earned $685 million from visitors in 2025 and registered $2.62 billion of new investment.

capital.heading: Rwanda borrows on reforms it can show. Next, a clean stove in every home.

record.text: IMF Extended Credit Facility, approved June 2026, 38 months
IMF Resilience and Sustainability Facility, completed December 2024
World Bank support to clean energy access (ASCENT)
Priority skills and youth employment, paid on results
World Bank finance for affordable housing

register.name: Extended Credit Facility
register.note: SDR 185.031 million; first review agreed at staff level, 6 October 2026
register.text: The first IMF lending arrangement since the Standby Credit Facility. Completion of the first review would release about $35.7 million.

register.name: Policy Coordination Instrument
register.note: A non-financing programme that signals policy to investors
register.text: Rwanda runs its reforms under an IMF instrument that lends nothing and certifies a great deal.

register.name: Resilience and Sustainability Facility
register.note: Long-term financing tied to climate reforms
register.text: One of the first RSF arrangements in the world, completed in full.

register.name: Standby Credit Facility
register.text: Short-term support approved alongside the PCI and RSF reviews, completed December 2024.

register.name: Accelerating Sustainable and Clean Energy Access Transformation
register.text: Extends electricity and clean cooking to households: the instrument closest to the guarantee that holds Rwanda lowest.

register.name: Commercialization and De-Risking for Agricultural Transformation
register.text: Draws private finance into farming and the businesses around it.

register.name: Priority Skills for Growth and Youth Empowerment
register.note: Skills and jobs for young people
register.text: Pays on verified results in technical training and youth employment.

register.name: Boosting Green Finance, Investment and Trade
register.text: Supports reforms that open Rwanda to green investment and trade.

register.name: Housing Finance Project
register.text: Builds the market for long-term, affordable home loans.

register.name: Health Emergency Preparedness, Response and Resilience
register.text: Strengthens the health system against outbreaks.

register.name: Social Protection Transformation Project
register.text: Modernises the cash transfer and public works system for the poorest households.

register.name: Stunting Prevention and Reduction, Additional Financing
register.text: Works to reduce stunting among young children.

assets.heading: Five assets no balance sheet counts.

items.name: The Hills
items.label: Of land in agriculture, 2024
items.text: Three-quarters of the land is farmed. Irrigation and markets, not more land, carry the next gain.

items.name: The Forest
items.label: Of land under forest, 2024
items.text: The forest holds the water for the hills below and the parks that visitors come for.

items.name: The Visitors
items.label: Tourism revenue, 2025
items.text: 1.49 million arrivals in 2025, up 9% on the year before.
items.alt: Visitors in a Rwandan national park

items.name: The Hub
items.label: Investment registered, 2025
items.text: Across 799 projects. A state that investors can read is itself an asset.

items.name: The People
items.label: Citizens, 2025
items.text: Three in ten live in towns and cities; the rest live on the hills they farm.

items.name: The enterprises building Perfect Rwanda
items.text: The Stewards are verifying the companies and social enterprises already delivering the seven basic living standards in Rwanda. Suggest one to include.

coverage.gap_text: Rwandans who cook without clean fuel or technology: nine in ten.

guarantees.name: Food
guarantees.note: Lenient measure: 22.6% are undernourished; food insecurity experience is not published

guarantees.name: Water
guarantees.note: Basic water; safely managed water is not measured

guarantees.name: Shelter
guarantees.note: Outside urban slums; 38.4% of city dwellers live in slums; safe sanitation not measured

guarantees.name: Energy
guarantees.note: 9% cook with clean fuels and technology

guarantees.name: Education
guarantees.note: Lower-secondary completion; reading data not published

guarantees.name: Livelihoods
guarantees.note: Above US$3.00 a day; 38.6% live below it
